newsitem.title: USA: Conn. comptroller ups surplus forecast by $70 mln.
newsitem.headline: Conn. comptroller ups surplus forecast by $70 mln.

text.p: Connecticut's general fund surplus for the fiscal year ending June 30 has grown to $268.4 million, about $70 million higher than previously forecast, comptroller Nancy Wyman projected Monday.
She said this was mainly a result of income tax collections running nine percent higher than last year.
Wyman said Connecticut will collect some $3.14 billion in income taxes this year -- $291 million more than the state budget planned for.
"This performance reflects solid state economic growth driven by a rapidly expanding national economy," Wyman said in her monthly report on the state's financial position.
Wyman also projected a transportation fund surplus of $110.94 million.

She called for using some measure of the surplus to reduce the state's per capita long-term debt, which is the highest in the nation. The legislature's appropriations committee has approved plans to use $166.7 million of the surplus to retire the remainder of the state's 1991 debt.
